This secondary implementation reference is for contributors. For a researcher
introduction, start with [semantic geometry](concepts/geometry.qmd) or the
[tutorials](examples.qmd). Repository procedures live in the
[maintainer entry](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim/blob/develop/MAINTAINING.md).

SCGSim keeps PDK facts, component intent, semantic geometry, solver preparation,
execution, result loading, and presentation distinguishable. A solver backend
may implement its own physics, but it must not redefine geometry identity, run
identity, or common provenance.

## Accepted SCGSim 2.0 structure

Human accepted the current v2 structural/API implementation on 2026-10-09:
candidate `a932a173edb5c56ae14740ff5177190996255bdd`, tree
`2745321736e53e2a4fe8d150f2e9d8bd176669db`. Its semantic state is `ACCEPTED`,
not `STABILIZED` or integrated. The migration baseline is
`develop@3a52fb1`, tree `96adcf8672b497a29dd0a6b43043cca11efc3043`; existing
consumer pins remain unchanged. The accepted Q3D body-v3 scope includes a
native build-only/readback/save/release operation, not a completed C/G solve.
The full Xmon Route A, CircularPad Route B, and HFSS Eigenmode/saved-field
EPR/offline-loss endpoints remain deferred; their partial observations are not
reported as full completion.

The accepted responsibility tree is:

```text
scgsim/
├── geometry/
│   ├── source/       # component input, occurrence, stack and normalization
│   ├── models/       # source and construction records
│   ├── compiler/     # advanced build API, derived records and validators
│   ├── planning/     # domain, interface, surface, volume and tag planning
│   ├── construction/ # native OCC construction, correspondence and export
│   └── _primitives/  # shared lower source/compiler operations
├── semantics/        # immutable solver-independent facts
├── palace/
│   ├── preparation/  # distinct Electrostatic and Eigenmode input state owners
│   ├── mesh/         # route build, Gmsh worker, summaries and offline quality
│   │   └── quality/  # detached offline MSH reader and report
│   ├── execution/    # manual handoff and host receipt recorder
│   ├── results/      # custody-aware result and EPR reading
│   └── presentation/ # Palace-specific reports and figures
├── aedt/
│   ├── eigenmode.py  # retained mutable high-level state facade
│   ├── specs/        # common and HFSS/Q2D/Q3D request records and parsing
│   ├── preparation/ # portable handoff, geometry and cohort membership
│   ├── runtime/     # sole transaction and family-native owners
│   ├── epr/         # EPR source geometry, fields/cache and workflow
│   ├── results/     # strict readers and convergence observations
│   ├── presentation/
│   └── run.py       # supported CLI, delegates to transaction owner
├── visualization/
│   ├── loaders/
│   ├── scene.py
│   ├── preview.py
│   └── rendering.py
└── presentation/     # shared physics-neutral notebook formatting
```

Only create a leaf when it owns real implementation. Geometry planning and
construction primitives have one shared lower-level owner; backend families
consume that geometry without importing one another. `semantics` remains a
stdlib-only immutable fact boundary. Palace and AEDT keep separate mutable
simulation state, transaction lifetime, and physical result meaning. Shared
presentation formats detached values; it does not own solver physics or
calculation. Visualization reads solver-authoritative metadata and artifacts;
it does not start a solve or determine run status.

Publicness follows explicit package facades, declared submodule exports and
documented contracts—not mere importability. The accepted v2 source keeps the
high-level `scgsim.geometry`, `scgsim.palace`, `scgsim.aedt`, and
`scgsim.visualization` entrypoints, and supplies an old-to-new submodule and
symbol map in the [API migration reference](api-migration.qmd). Moved private
implementations do not gain public status by relocation. There will be one
current implementation, without old `scgsim.sgb` compatibility wrappers or
revived Q3D input-v1/v2 paths. The formal `python -m scgsim.aedt.run` entrypoint
remains supported; it is the AEDT transaction CLI, not a legacy wrapper.

The geometry facade is source-facing: it owns component/occurrence and stack
adaptation, `GeometryPlan` and detached snapshots, normalized input records,
vacuum/curve declarations and input summaries. `scgsim.geometry.compiler` is
the advanced builder, derived-record and stage-validation surface. Input-only
`validate_geometry_input` is defined below the compiler in
`scgsim.geometry.source.validation` and re-exported by the compiler facade. Shared
loop, spatial and Entity primitives sit below both source and compiler, so
source preparation does not depend on planning. The compiler/construction
boundary retains native correspondence, stock CAD shell repair, curved
arrangement and XAO/physical-group behavior. The full source-facing and
advanced symbol paths, including direct model aliases and pipeline validators,
are listed in the [API migration reference](api-migration.qmd).

Palace keeps two distinct mutable preparation owners: Electrostatic and
Eigenmode setup state, invalidation, and failure ordering remain specific to
each facade. Mesh construction retains its dynamic Gmsh worker boundary and
native observation; offline mesh-quality reading stays separate. Manual
handoff and its standalone host recorder remain execution-owned, while strict
result/EPR resolution remains offline and Palace reports remain
solver-specific. AEDT likewise keeps its `EigenmodeSim` state facade, but one
runtime transaction owns receipt transitions and the sole Desktop lifecycle;
family runtimes own native prepare/solve/export/readback. EPR preparation and
saved-field analysis stay in their EPR workflow, strict resolution does not
execute a solver, and presentation consumes detached results. These are
separate ownership boundaries, not shared solver base classes.

Within Palace, `results.report_data` owns detached report records and snapshot
readers; `presentation.reports` owns trust/physics views and figures. The
package facade retains the existing public result and report names.

For the Q3D termination-and-save candidate, the AEDT producer advances to
`scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v14` with 62 canonical declared module paths,
adding `scgsim/aedt/runtime/control.py` to the frozen V13 inventory of 61
paths, including 41 AEDT modules. V14 records carry `schema_version`, `stage`,
`modules`, `content_sha256`, and
`revision_observation`; module bytes and their digest are mandatory, while the
truthful Git observation may be unavailable. V14 has no helper-hash map and
does not claim exhaustive transitive-source coverage. Historical runtime-source
v1–v13 continue to interpret their original module paths and identities; V14
does not rewrite or reinterpret historical receipts.

The flow below shows the accepted source structure. Geometry source preparation
and compiler planning have separate owners, and neither backend defines source
identity.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  PDK["PDK material, layer, fabrication, and host semantics"] --> PLAN["Notebook GeometryPlan"]
  COMPONENT["Local component entities, polygon/curve boundaries, ports, selectors"] --> PLAN
  NOTEBOOK["Named occurrences and final Net → Entity map"] --> PLAN
  PLAN --> SNAPSHOT["Immutable source snapshot"]
  SNAPSHOT --> INPUT["Normalized GeometryBuildInput"]
  INPUT --> SOURCE["scgsim.geometry source API"]
  SOURCE --> COMPILER["scgsim.geometry.compiler"]
  INPUT --> AEDT["AEDT native geometry and bindings"]
  COMPILER --> PALACE["Palace backend preparation"]
  PALACE --> HANDOFF["Run-and-handoff contracts"]
  AEDT --> HANDOFF
  HANDOFF --> PROFILE["Selected machine profile"]
  PROFILE --> ARTIFACTS["Immutable artifacts and receipts"]
  ARTIFACTS --> RESULTS["Solver-specific physical results"]
  RESULTS --> REPORT["Unified Plotly report envelope"]
```

The current geometry implementation starts from component-local source facts and
named occurrences. A `GeometryPlan` holds the expanded entity inventory and
the Notebook's final `Net -> Entity` map, then prepares one immutable source
snapshot for the normalized `GeometryBuildInput` boundary. The accepted 1.1.0
source model includes authored curve declarations and explicit GDS
reconstruction records in that snapshot while preserving Entity/Net ownership.
`scgsim.geometry` owns the source-facing plan and snapshot; the
`scgsim.geometry.compiler` surface owns route planning and derived construction
records. Palace consumes curve intent through this compiler; AEDT curve
lowering is unsupported. The
[GeometryPlan contract](geometry-sgb.qmd) owns exact curve identity and
arrangement semantics. Native observations do not replace source identity or
establish connectivity. AEDT binding evidence retains source members and
coverage through native aggregation.

On the Palace OCC path, stock shell AutoFix may replace native face tags while
correcting shell orientation. Geometry construction maps repaired faces to source surfaces by
complete native wire/edge correspondence and carries that mapping through
export and backend construction. Source `SurfaceID`s remain authoritative;
numeric Gmsh tags may change. In the observed Circle Route B construction,
shared faces and metal-cutout boundaries remained source-bound, with port
sheets still separate. That observation is scoped to this geometry case. Construction fails
when required correspondence cannot be established. The geometry contract
owns the exact behavior and failure boundary.

## Contract boundaries

| Boundary | Authority |
|---|---|
| Material, layer, fabrication, Z/thickness, and 3D host facts | PDK |
| Local entities, polygon and authored curve boundaries, ports, and topology selectors | Component designer |
| Named occurrences and the final `Net -> Entity` assignment | Notebook `GeometryPlan` |
| Immutable normalized source geometry | `GeometryPlan` and `GeometryBuildInput` |
| Revision-bound material, interface, owner, side, and evidence facts | `scgsim.semantics` internal stdlib core |
| Geometry names, topology, Route A/B surfaces | `scgsim.geometry.compiler` |
| Palace and AEDT implementation | `scgsim.palace` and `scgsim.aedt` |
| Native geometry bindings and derived aggregates | Backend adapters, with source members and coverage retained |
| Solver-bound geometry inspection and preview evidence | `scgsim.visualization` |
| Run identity, handoff, profiles, receipts | One common SCGSim contract |
| Physical result meaning | Solver-specific, never flattened into a false common quantity |
| Report navigation, provenance, cost presentation | SCGSim report/resolver surfaces |
| Offline tetrahedral mesh diagnostics | `scgsim.palace.mesh.quality`, exposed through `scgsim.palace` |
| Public component-simulation notebook source | OrPen SC PDK |

## Internal semantic facts

`scgsim.semantics` is a solver-independent stdlib boundary. It detaches plain
values into recursively immutable, revision-bound snapshots and returns detached
serialization. Evidence patches retain the snapshot that classified them;
missing/different revision identity fails rather than silently rebinding facts.
Native tags remain opaque observations, not sources of guessed contact.

The geometry compiler reuses one source/model projection while planning instead of deep-copying
stacks at every adjacency call. Domain ordering, sheet owners and aggregate
physical-group owners remain separate projections. Contribution multiplicity
is retained by the semantic ledger even when native geometry aggregates a
surface. Material identity, approximation and native implementation stay
separate. The [GeometryPlan/route contract](geometry-sgb.qmd) owns their public
meaning; this page explains which modules implement it.

AEDT's native construction does not consume Gmsh tags or construction plans.
Its binding sidecar retains source members and coverage through native bodies,
sheets, faces and calculator selections. The [AEDT contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd)
owns exact side-selection and result rules. Display-only helpers live under
`scgsim.aedt.presentation`, with public methods delegating to them; presentation
adds no solver execution or shared physics schema.

## Notebook and implementation boundaries

OrPen SC PDK owns the public component examples and calls the shared runtime
directly. SCGSim owns the reusable package APIs, not a duplicate notebook source.

The per-family supported calculations and current limits
are maintained in the [Backend Support Matrix](backend-support.qmd).

Palace mesh-quality inspection is an offline reader under
`scgsim.palace.mesh.quality` over the emitted MSH file.
It neither owns mesh construction nor starts a native backend. The reader binds
one immutable parsed snapshot to the file bytes and leaves mesh acceptance and
scientific convergence outside the report contract. See
[Tetrahedral Mesh Quality](mesh-quality.qmd).

## Palace preparation lifecycle

`ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` remain the public owners of their mutable
mesh, config, resolved-port, and handoff state. Their shared private workflow
only prepares values and persists caller-supplied JSON payloads; it is not a
base simulation object and does not receive callbacks into simulation state.

Both public `mesh()` methods invalidate derived state before checking
prerequisites. Geometry preparation then applies the existing vacuum, Route-A,
and indium-bump transformations in order and returns the prepared component,
stack, bump-fill record, and optional material mapping before airbox lowering.
The simulation conditionally stores that mapping at the existing point, so an
earlier transform failure or a non-mapping `materials` value retains the prior
mapping, while an airbox or mesh-construction failure retains the newly prepared
mapping. Eigenmode resolves authored ports before those transformations and
caches the resolved ports only after mesh construction succeeds.

Both public `write_config()` methods invalidate config and handoff state before
their existing prerequisite and mesh-existence checks. Solver-specific lowering
still occurs before persistence. A shared private writer replaces each
caller-ordered metadata file independently and replaces `config.json` last;
earlier files therefore remain after a later write failure, and `config_path` is
cached only after the final replacement succeeds. In-memory invalidation does
not remove an older config file from disk, and this per-file behavior is not a
whole-workflow transaction guarantee.

The shared stack loader, non-negative-number validator, and stack-material-kind
validator live in `scgsim.palace.preparation.inputs`. Electrostatic and
Eigenmode call that module directly while retaining their public methods,
invalidation timing, shallow top-level stack copy, nested aliases, and
problem-specific orchestration. The old direct problem-module paths were
removed; their current defining modules are `preparation.electrostatic` and
`preparation.eigenmode`.

The accepted 1.1.0 Palace mesh behavior separates Gmsh geometric order from FEM
order and keeps the Delaunay/HXT choice, thread settings and high-order
optimization outcome with the generated mesh. `mesh_summary()` returns detached
meshing evidence bound to the mesh and manifest identities; Palace report and
resolved-result views read the same recorded authority. The Eigenmode summary's
topological degree-of-freedom estimate is not an actual solver degree-of-freedom
count, and Electrostatic does not claim an unavailable H1 estimate. These mesh
and summary additions are ACCEPTED.

## AEDT execution lifecycle

`scgsim.aedt.run` remains the supported command-line entrypoint and delegates
to `scgsim.aedt.runtime.transaction.main`, the owner of the AEDT transaction,
receipt transitions, and Desktop lifecycle. The transaction validates one
prepared handoff before changing its receipt, imports PyAEDT only after that
transition, opens and releases the owned Desktop, dispatches one solver family,
and gives the original family failure precedence over a later release failure.
Private HFSS, Q3D, and Q2D modules each own their native model
preparation, explicit solve, and export/readback stages. Families do not import
the transaction module, and their narrow shared native helpers do not import a
family or start a Desktop.

The Q3D user-requested Stop/Abort-and-save scope remains `CONVERGING`; native
operations are unobserved. It exposes
`request_q3d_stop_and_save(handoff)` for Clean Stop after the current pass and
`request_q3d_abort_and_save(handoff)` to interrupt current work, with exclusive
CLI flags `--stop-and-save` and `--abort-and-save`. Both use one exact-target
local-Linux requester, the owned Desktop and transaction identity/nonce, and
the shared control ledger/lock. Repeating the same mode is idempotent; a
conflicting committed mode is refused without another native RPC. Raw RPC
responses are uninterpreted. Linux stop-managed Q3D refuses PyAEDT
documentation mode before Desktop creation because it overrides the close
flags needed for exclusive transaction ownership.

The recorder retains blocking Analyze, then observes native
`odesktop.AreThereSimulationsRunning(True)` once; `True` includes pending
simulations and only native `False` confirms inactivity. Active, unknown, or
unavailable state, or uncertain control-ledger closure/read/write/readback,
fails and preserves the Desktop by non-closing detach with `release.ok=false`,
defers Save/export, and writes no post-release seal or success status. With confirmed inactivity and known ledger state, the recorder attempts
explicit Save first, independently records requested available completed-result
matrix/convergence exports, retains any raw native files actually produced,
and records errors separately. It closes/releases the Desktop only if that
Save succeeds. Save failure yields
`release.ok=false` with reason `save_failed` and a non-closing detach; it leaves
the project/Desktop preserved, with no seal or automatic cleanup.
Optional artifacts do not promise recovery or completeness for interrupted
work, and their errors do not define the Stop/Abort-save workflow status.
`normal_stop_saved` and `abort_saved` require the matching committed intent,
returned RPC, Analyze true, confirmed inactivity, successful explicit
Save/release, and post-release seal. They label finalized workflows, not
physics completion or causal proof. Analyze false/exception stays primary with
causality unknown; RPC, control-mode, ACF, Save/export, and release errors stay
separately visible. Strict completed-result resolution and Report remain
unchanged; there is no partial-result surface. Ordinary no-intent Q3D, other
solver families, and non-Linux solver flows are unchanged.

At family entry, one private bound request fixes the absolute run workspace and
detaches the parsed spec payload. Relative source paths are interpreted against
that bound workspace even if the process working directory later changes;
absolute source paths retain their authored lexical identity. Preparation reads
only this bound request after entry. Its carrier retains the mutable native app
handle together with detached preparation readback; solve and export consume the
carrier and cannot reinterpret a caller spec or workspace.

In this candidate, new preparation keeps the handoff and handoff-manifest
schemas at V1 while both declare that the mutable run receipt uses
`scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3`. The initial
V3 receipt records a declared `runtime-source.v14` preparation-time SCGSim module
manifest and content digest. Before mutation, execution verifies the canonical
manifest and binds the initial-receipt and prepared-manifest hashes. A canonical historical
V1 `not_run` handoff with neither marker remains executable, but its resulting
V3 receipt records preparation provenance as `legacy_v1_not_recorded`; it does
not fabricate history.

Every new completed V3 receipt in this candidate records a separate declared
`runtime-source.v14` execution-time module manifest and digest. Its measured
module bytes and
content digest are mandatory; it has no helper-hash map. Preparation and
execution identities are not required to match: their separation records what
prepared and what actually executed the handoff. Historical completed V1
receipts remain subject to their old resolution rules, except that a V1 receipt
combined with either later-version expectation marker is rejected as an
inconsistent cohort. Historical completed V2 receipts retain their existing
resolution rules; new V3-only native PEC checks do not reinterpret them. This
consistency contract is not source authenticity for an actor able
to rewrite the entire unsigned artifact set.

The [AEDT receipt/provenance contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#receipt-cohorts-and-source-provenance)
is the unique authority for the exact current V14 inventory and frozen
historical reader evolution. V1–V13 retain their exact prior path assignments
and reader interpretations; V14 binds its declared file set, not every
transitive dependency. One pure, versioned initial-receipt codec owns historical
V1/V2 and current V3 JSON member order, indentation and final newline; handoff
writing and initial-receipt reconstruction use that codec. Historical receipt
hashes are never compared with installed source, and preparation and execution
identities remain independent evidence.

Runtime-source provenance is computed inside the receipt-owned failure
transaction before PyAEDT import and Desktop construction. New HFSS V3 receipts
also keep source material identity distinct from verified native PEC
implementation: solids are native `pec` with Solve Inside disabled, while
sheets receive Perfect E and must have complete native face coverage.

The accepted Eigenmode EPR lifecycle is an explicit additive path under that
same transaction owner. It does not reinterpret the historical one-shot
prepare--solve--export path or broaden the meaning of an ordinary completed
receipt. Before its one solve, the EPR path declares geometry bindings,
junctions, contributions, margins, calculator definitions, and native pass
cache items. After the solver stops it exports the recorded pass/mode history;
if the solve raises or returns failure, the transaction preserves that original
error, releases the owned Desktop, and performs no automatic save or partial
export recovery. The existing complete-convergence reader remains unchanged;
history exported after a successful solve records its own completed pass
identities and status.

Mode selection is postprocessing state, not a physical design variation. A
complete Eigenmode source vector selects exactly one native mode with the
dimensionless relative control `1`, with every other mode `0`, and binds phase
and the selected solution explicitly. `EigenPeakElectricField` names the
native normalization convention; this control is not a measured `1 V/m` field.
The vector order and persisted native source entries are evidence; inherited
GUI state and a synthetic `Mode` intrinsic are not. Pass-cache identity
separately binds setup, physical variation, adaptive pass, native mode, item
definition, dependencies, context, and solution. Item titles and row positions
are never identity.

Historical cache resolution and final saved-field analysis are independent
capabilities. The history reader returns only the pass/mode values that AEDT
actually recorded, preserving axes and missingness. Final analysis closes and
seals the solved project plus its complete result directory, reopens a distinct
working copy with solve guards installed, and evaluates the last saved fields
without modifying the original. Missing final fields do not fall back to an
earlier cache pass, and a new postsolve margin is a final-field calculation,
not invented pass history.

See [Folder tree and ownership](ownership.qmd) for repository placement and
[Headless Geometry Preview](geometry-preview.qmd) for the static and connected
Notebook inspection contract.
